card.intuition: Contextual knowledge is facts the agent can read directly from the context window right now — the user's task, files read in, tool results, and AGENTS.md loaded at session start. It is the counterpart to parametric knowledge: parametric is recalled from frozen parameters, contextual is read from the window, and hallucinations are much less common when the answer is in front of the model.
card.analogy: A memo pinned to your monitor instead of something you memorized. Recalling is unreliable for things you rarely saw (parametric); reading the memo is reliable — provided it is in the room. But every memo costs desk space, so pin only the relevant ones, not the whole filing cabinet.
card.time_complexity: O(C) per decoded token over the full context window — contextual knowledge is read from the window, so loading more facts costs linearly more per request.
card.space_complexity: Context/memory footprint: contextual knowledge lives in the window and spends tokens, and everything loaded competes for the model's finite attention budget, so loading more is not automatically better.
when_to_use: Supplying knowledge the parameters lack: an internal SDK, a library released after the cutoff, or a decision made yesterday
Pasting current API docs so the model follows them rather than its stale memory of the old API
Explaining API behavior: with the docs in it is contextual knowledge, without them it is parametric and the rare endpoints blur
Restating a correction or moving it closer to the work when stale parametric patterns leak through
gotchas: Contextual knowledge costs tokens and competes for attention budget — the aim is the relevant facts in the window, not all the facts
Do not call it 'working memory': contextual knowledge is what is in the window now, while a memory system is what moves cross-session content into it
The old parametric version can still bleed through in a long session even with docs loaded; restating the correction helps

exercise.prompt: Classify which knowledge source answers a fact: contextual when it is read from the loaded window, otherwise parametric.
hints: Contextual knowledge is whatever is present in the window at the moment it is needed.
Check membership of the fact in the loaded_window list to decide the source.
exercise.test_code:
assert knowledge_source('parseAsync', ['parseAsync docs'], {}) == 'contextual'
assert knowledge_source('parseAsync', [], {'parseAsync': 'old'}) == 'parametric'
assert knowledge_source('parseAsync', ['other docs'], {'parseAsync': 'old'}) == 'parametric'
print('PASS')
